name: blackswan-orderflow
description: The ORDER-FLOW (taker-imbalance) probe — the second NON-PRICE stream in the project, and the cheapest possible one: the aggressor split is ALREADY in the on-disk 1m klines (asset_volume_taker_base = the volume where the taker was the buyer), so no data is mined. Per bar the signed imbalance is (2*taker_buy - volume)/volume in [-1,+1] — net aggressive buying above 0, net selling below. This backtest asks whether conditioning a directional trade on an EXTREME of that imbalance beats buy-and-hold NET of the ~0.2% crypto round trip: flow_momentum RIDES the extreme (informed aggressor flow persists), flow_contrarian FADES it (aggressors overpay the spread and get run over). It reuses the intraday backtest mechanics and the shared past-only extreme core (signal_extremes), so every existing gate, lens and scorecard reads a flow cell unchanged. Guards pinned before any number is emitted: (a) imbalance is built from ONLY a bar's own minutes (no straddle) and is the SIGNED aggressor ratio — all-buy=+1, all-sell=-1, balanced=0, zero-volume=None; (b) the imbalance measured over bar t is known at t's close and the position it implies is applied to bars t+1.. never bar t's own return, and positions never read price at all; (c) 'is this imbalance extreme?' is judged against the PAST-ONLY imbalance distribution (a whole-sample quantile would fabricate the signal). Deterministic and model-free (the seed is contract-only). flow_coverage is emitted so a broken aggregation surfaces as a metric, not a silent all-flat book.

asset.description: Which crypto instrument's 1m taker-split is aggregated and whose price is traded and benchmarked. return_vs_hold_pct and beta/up/down capture are measured against THIS asset over the same span.

bar.description: Decision-bar width in minutes: the 1m taker-split is aggregated up to this cadence and the imbalance + every trade decision is taken on these bars. Smaller bars fire more often (raising trades_per_day) and pay the cost floor more often — the central tension. Bar widths that divide the day evenly keep aggregation exact across month boundaries.

signal.description: The reading of a taker-imbalance extreme. flow_momentum RIDES it — long a net-buying extreme, short a net-selling extreme — on the thesis that aggressive (informed) flow persists. flow_contrarian FADES it, on the thesis that aggressors overpay the spread and get run over. A bar fires only when its imbalance is at/above the flow_pct quantile (or at/below 1-flow_pct) of the PAST-ONLY imbalance distribution. An unknown value is refused, so a typo can never file one arm's result under the other's label.

flow_pct.description: The quantile of the TRAILING (expanding, past-only) imbalance distribution at/above which a bar is a net-buying extreme (and at/below 1-this a net-selling extreme). Computed only from imbalance observed at prior bars — a whole-sample quantile would be a silent lookahead. Higher values demand a rarer, more lopsided flow (fewer trades).

hold_bars.description: How many decision bars a position is held after entry, then flat. The position earns bars t+1..t+hold_bars (never the signal bar's own return), and a new extreme inside the hold window is ignored.

transaction_fee.description: Per-side fee, charged on turnover at entry and again at exit, so a round trip costs ~(1-fee)^2 ≈ 0.2% at the default — the crypto cost floor this probe is measured against.

walk_forward_window.description: Which out-of-sample span is ACCOUNTED. Only the test window's bars enter the metrics and the benchmark; the month before it is loaded solely to warm the past-only imbalance distribution. alt-* windows suit the altcoins whose 1m history starts in 2022; alt-2024 and alt-2025 are the two fully-mined crypto windows shared by all three assets.

seed.description: Present for contract conformance only — the backtest is fully deterministic, so seeds are not swept (identical cells would fake replication).
